classification.difficultyReason: Uses differentiation and trigonometric simplification to derive the vertex, then determines the launch angle from maximum height.

content.prompt:
A particle is projected from the origin with initial speed $V$ at angle $\theta$ to the horizontal.

You may assume the equation of its parabolic path is $y=x\tan\theta-\dfrac{gx^2\sec^2\theta}{2V^2}$. Use $g=10\text{ m/s}^2$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$, and hence show that the vertex of the parabola is $\left(\dfrac{V^2\sin 2\theta}{2g},\dfrac{V^2\sin^2\theta}{2g}\right)$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{dy}{dx}&=\tan\theta-\frac{gx\sec^2\theta}{V^2}.\end{align*}$$
At the vertex, $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=0$.
$$\begin{align*}\tan\theta-\frac{gx\sec^2\theta}{V^2}&=0\\x&=\frac{V^2\tan\theta}{g\sec^2\theta}\\x&=\frac{V^2\sin 2\theta}{2g}.\end{align*}$$
Substitute into the equation for $y$:
$$\begin{align*}y_{\text{vertex}}&=\frac{V^2\sin 2\theta}{2g}\tan\theta-\left(\frac{V^2\sin 2\theta}{2g}\right)^2\frac{g\sec^2\theta}{2V^2}\\y_{\text{vertex}}&=\frac{V^2\cdot2\sin\theta\cos\theta}{2g}\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}-\frac{V^4\cdot4\sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta}{4g^2}\frac{g}{2V^2\cos^2\theta}\\y_{\text{vertex}}&=\frac{V^2\sin^2\theta}{g}-\frac{V^2\sin^2\theta}{2g}\\y_{\text{vertex}}&=\frac{V^2\sin^2\theta}{2g}.\end{align*}$$
Hence the vertex is $\left(\dfrac{V^2\sin 2\theta}{2g},\dfrac{V^2\sin^2\theta}{2g}\right)$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: If $V=20\text{ m/s}$ and the greatest height is $15\text{ m}$, find $\theta$.
